screen_html.probe: every tick reads the verb off the live adapter, never a version number (_html_verb): the public edit_message when inspect.signature shows a parameter named parse_mode (positional-or-keyword or keyword-only; **kwargs does not count), else the adapter's own coroutine _edit_text, else none. The HTML form goes through that verb (edit_message(chat, message_id, html, parse_mode='HTML') and its SendResult, or _edit_text(chat, message_id, html, 'HTML') which raises on refusal); on any refusal other than 'not modified' the same tick edits plain through the public edit_message. Plain succeeded right after HTML failed = the HTML form was refused: screen_format 'plain', the reason in html_error (the exception class, or 'edit_message: <error>'), HTML tried again after HTML_RETRY_TICKS (12). No verb at all = plain, html_error 'no HTML verb (edit_message without parse_mode, no _edit_text)'. The record names the verb that carries the HTML: html_verb 'edit_message' | '_edit_text' | null
screen_html.contract: TelegramAdapter.edit_message(self, chat_id, message_id, content, *, finalize=False, metadata=None) -> SendResult: no parse_mode on any engine known today; without finalize it calls _edit_text(chat_id, message_id, content), plain text. TelegramAdapter._edit_text(self, chat_id: str, message_id: str, text: str, parse_mode: Any = None) -> None: normalizes the ids, passes parse_mode to Bot.edit_message_text only when given, raises the PTB error on refusal ('Message is not modified' included). A PRIVATE method: the plugin treats it as a capability, never as a promise, asks the public verb's signature first (the catalog review's order) and keeps the plain public edit as the fallback. The parse mode is the string 'HTML' (ParseMode.HTML is that string); the markup is <b> and one <blockquote expandable>, both Bot API 7.4+, not the rich_message parameter

external_limits.probe: limits_sources in the config, a list of up to 4 entries checked when the settings are read: url http on loopback (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]) without credentials; key_env a variable name that is not a bot token variable (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, HERMES_DASHBOARD_BOT_TOKEN, any *_BOT_TOKEN in any case); timeout_seconds 1..120, default 20. A refused entry is 'no data' with its reason and is never requested; limits_enabled off = no sources
external_limits.contract: contract 1 (README, External limit sources): GET <url> with Accept application/json and an optional Authorization Bearer from key_env; 200, a JSON object of at most 64 KB with contract, provider, state ok|login_expired|unavailable, reason, plan, login_expires_at, fetched_at, windows[] (up to 6: used_percent, resets_at, scope, severity, label); unknown keys ignored, every string sanitized. No proxy from the environment, no redirect, the body of an error answer unread. The tick waits 25 s; the request runs on in its own worker (one per source) with timeout_seconds; on a miss the last line with its own stamp while younger than two ticks or two limits_refresh_seconds. One attempt per limits_refresh_seconds, cache in the plugin record under external_cache (external.py, collect.py)
external_limits.caveat: no engine import and no engine surface: the row depends on the local process that answers, not on the Hermes version, so no version is listed. Pinned by tests/test_external.py against a real local HTTP server and by an answer captured from a real contract-1 source on 2026-09-28; not yet live on a gateway

gemini_log.probe: HERMES_HOME/logs/ is a directory: no directory = unsupported; the directory without errors.log = fresh with no 429 (the engine on Windows creates the file at the first WARNING); a file that cannot be read or is not UTF-8 = unavailable, the line keeps the last 429 the record remembers; limits_enabled off = not read
reads: the whole of logs/errors.log on the first read, if the file is at most 4 MB and decodes as UTF-8 (every read is a first read until one succeeds and leaves last_429 in the record, null when nothing was seen); otherwise, and after that, its last 256 KB, from the first whole line to the last
the stamp, level and logger of every entry header
for an entry whose first line holds Gemini and HTTP 429: limit: N, model: X and retry in N s of its message, the traceback excluded
entries within 10 s of the newest as one refusal
never_reads: the text of a message beyond those three fields
gemini_log.contract: hermes_logging.py: errors.log holds WARNING and above, rotated at 2 MB with 2 backups (:196), UTF-8, format '%(asctime)s %(levelname)s%(session_tag)s %(name)s: %(message)s' (:47), the stamp naive in the host's local time. The text-to-speech 429: ERROR tools.tts_tool 'TTS generation failed (gemini): Gemini TTS API error (HTTP 429): <error.message>' with its traceback (tools/tts_tool.py:310-314, tools/tts_tool_providers.py:603), repeated within the same second by the executor's WARNING cut at 200 characters (agent/tool_executor.py:994) and the voice reply's WARNING (gateway/run_voice.py:342); the LLM path: WARNING agent.conversation_loop 'API call failed ... summary=Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): ...' (agent/turn_recovery.py:916-919, agent/gemini_native_adapter.py:628); the streamed call: ERROR agent.chat_completion_helpers 'Streaming failed before delivery: Gemini HTTP 429 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED): ...' with its traceback (agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:3150), beside the turn loop's WARNING 'Retrying API call in Ns' (agent/turn_recovery.py:1091-1095), the engine's own backoff and not Google's retry. QuotaFailure and RetryInfo are dropped by the engine: only the message is logged. The last 429 is kept in the plugin record (gemini_log_cache); a retry over 120 s is the daily quota, an event until the reset; any other 429 marks the line for an hour; no network (gemini_log.py)

gemini_log.caveat: only the engine's own calls are in that log: a script that calls Gemini on its own, such as a skill's, is not seen. The stamp is converted with the process's own zone, so the hour repeated when summer time ends adds an hour to the age of a 429 from that hour. The engine on Windows opens the file lazily: until the first WARNING there is no file, which reads as no 429. A daily quota spent just before Google's reset asks for a short retry and marks the line only
